title: Kiaull
description: Ten short stories about music: a pianist and her old ebony piano, an amateur band in a recording studio, a young ballet dancer with bruised toes, the opera with the magic flute, an old ballad about a siege, a music night in an inn by a fishing harbour, a composer listening to a meadow, a theremin built for school, a letter from an anthropologist recording songs in the tropics, and a rabbi and a lexicographer in the library.

lessons.title: Y pianneyder as y naighteyr
lessons.summary: Thomasina Brackenbury, a skilful pianist in Douglas, will play in a big hall on Tuesday; the journalist Esmond Fairfax visits her to write about her: she plays an old wooden piano with ebony keys and decorations on its wooden case, which her grandmother bought in London; her small house has little room, but the hall has room for five hundred people; she sits on her grandmother's old stool; a radio presenter will speak before she plays, and on Tuesday the hall is full.
lessons.text:
Ta Thomasina Brackenbury ny pianneyder. T'ee cummal ayns thie beg ayns Doolish. Jemayrt, bee ee cloie ayns thie mooar 'sy valley. Bee kiaull jeh Bach as Chopin ayn.

Ta Esmond Fairfax ny naighteyr. T'eh screeu son pabyr-naight ayns Doolish. Er y Jerdein roish shen, haink y naighteyr gys thie Thomasina. Va feyshtyn echey son y pianneyder.

Ayns y thie eck, va pianney mooar. She pianney fuyghagh v'ayn, as v'eh feer shenn. Va ny mairyn baney, as va ny mairyn doo jeant jeh eabban.

“Vel oo cloie er y phianney shoh dy chooilley laa?” dooyrt y naighteyr.

“Ta,” dooyrt Thomasina. “Chionnee my shenn-voir eh ayns Lunnin, keead bleeaney er dy henney. Ta'n eabban doo foast aalin. Jeeagh er y jesheenys er y chishtey fuyghagh!”

Va jesheenys aalin er y phianney: blaaghyn as duillagyn, giarit ayns y fuygh. Ren y naighteyr y jesheenys y choontey: va three blaaghyn jeig ayn.

Va'n thie beg, as cha row rheamys mooar ayn. Va'n pianney goaill ayrn mooar jeh'n rheamys. “Cha nel rheamys aym son pianney noa,” dooyrt Thomasina, as ren ee gearey.

Ren ee soie er stoyl beg roish y phianney. She stoyl fuyghagh v'ayn neesht. “Va'n stoyl shoh ec my shenn-voir,” dooyrt ee. “Cha jean mee cloie er stoyl elley.”

Eisht ren ee cloie arrane beg da'n naighteyr. Va ny laueyn eck tappee as aghtal. Ren y naighteyr eaishtagh, as cha dooyrt eh fockle.

“T'ou feer aghtal,” dooyrt eh ec y jerrey.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Thomasina. “Ta mee cloie dy chooilley laa, shen ooilley. T'ou uss aghtal er screeu.”

“Vel rheamys ayns y thie mooar son ymmodee sleih?” dooyrt eh.

“Ta. Ta rheamys ayn son queig cheead dy 'leih. Bee cuirreyder veih'n radio ayn neesht. Bee'n cuirreyder loayrt ec y toshiaght, roish y kiaull.”

Jemayrt, va'n thie mooar lane. Ren y cuirreyder loayrt mychione Thomasina, as eisht ren ee soie er y stoyl. Ren ee cloie rish daa oor. Lurg shen, ren y sleih ooilley bwoalley nyn laueyn.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta Thomasina Brackenbury?
She pianneyder ee, as t'ee cummal ayns Doolish.
Cre ta Esmond Fairfax jannoo?
She naighteyr eh. T'eh screeu son pabyr-naight.
Cre ta jeant jeh eabban?
Ta ny mairyn doo er y phianney jeant jeh eabban.
Cre va'n jesheenys er y phianney?
Va blaaghyn as duillagyn giarit ayns y fuygh.
Vel rheamys mooar ayns thie Thomasina?
Cha nel. Ta'n thie beg, as ta'n pianney goaill ayrn mooar jeh'n rheamys.
Cre ren y cuirreyder Jemayrt?
Ren y cuirreyder loayrt mychione Thomasina ec y toshiaght, roish y kiaull.

lessons.title: Y bann 'sy seyrlan
lessons.summary: Florian Halliwell and his friends have an amateur band in Ramsey; Verena Barnwell does the singing; they want to record a series of five songs in a studio, but their budget is small: three hundred pounds; the studio owner Giles Winthrop makes a bargain with them, a cheaper price on Sunday; they borrow a better guitar from a neighbour; Giles spurs Verena on to sing with more expression, and after eight hours together they have their five songs.
lessons.text:
Ta bann beg ec Florian Halliwell ayns Rhumsaa. Ta kiare caarjyn 'sy vann: Florian, as eshyn cloie y gitar; Verena Barnwell, as ish goaill arraneyn; as daa ghooinney aeg elley. She bann amateyragh t'ayn. Ta obbyr elley oc ooilley 'sy laa, as t'ad cloie kiaull cooidjagh 'syn astyr.

Ta Verena jannoo yn arraneys. Ta coraa lajer eck. Ta'n arraneys eck feer vie, ga dy vel ee amateyragh.

Ta'n bann laccal driaght dy arraneyn y recortey: queig arraneyn, cooidjagh er un recort. Agh t'ad laccal goll gys seyrlan son shen. Ta seyrlan ayns Doolish, as she Giles Winthrop ta reayll eh.

Cha nel y bushaid oc mooar. Ta three cheead punt oc, as cha nel ny smoo oc. Hie Florian gys y seyrlan, as dooyrt eh rish Giles: “Shoh yn bushaid ain. Vel shen dy liooar?”

Smooinee Giles. “Cha nel,” dooyrt eh. “Agh nee'm barganey riu. Cha nel peiagh erbee 'sy seyrlan Jedoonee. My nee shiu çheet Jedoonee, bee eh three cheead punt son y laa slane.”

“Shen barganey mie!” dooyrt Florian.

Agh va gitar Florian shenn as boght. Ren naboo echey gitar noa y eeassaghey da. “Foddee oo y gitar y eeassaghey son y Jedoonee,” dooyrt y naboo, “agh cur erash eh Jemayrt.”

Er y Jedoonee, haink y bann gys y seyrlan. Ren ad cloie cooidjagh, as ren Verena yn arraneys. Agh va Giles eaishtagh, as cha row eh booiagh.

“Ta'n coraa ayd mie,” dooyrt eh rish Verena, “agh cha nel dreagh ayn. Smooinee er ny focklyn. Ta'n arrane shoh trimshagh. Lhig da'n dreagh trimshagh çheet ayns dty choraa.”

Ren Giles brasnaghey ee reesht as reesht. “Reesht! Ny smoo dreagh!” Cha row Verena booiagh, agh va'n brasnaghey mie er e son. Ren eh brasnaghey ee dy ghoaill arrane ny share. Va'n nah arrane ny share, as va'n trass fer ny share foast.

Va ad 'sy seyrlan rish hoght ooryn. Ec y jerrey, va'n driaght dy arraneyn recortit.

“Va'n bushaid beg,” dooyrt Florian, “agh she recort mie t'ayn.”

Hug eh y gitar erash da'n naboo Jemayrt. Va'n bann amateyragh booiagh.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta jannoo yn arraneys 'sy vann?
Ta Verena Barnwell jannoo yn arraneys.
Cre'n bushaid va ec y vann?
Va three cheead punt oc.
Cre'n barganey ren Giles?
Dooyrt eh dy beagh eh three cheead punt son y laa slane Jedoonee.
Cre ren y naboo eeassaghey da Florian?
Ren y naboo gitar noa y eeassaghey da.
Cre dooyrt Giles mychione dreagh Verena?
Dooyrt eh nagh row dreagh ayns y choraa eck.
Cre'n driaght dy arraneyn ren y bann recortey?
Ren ad queig arraneyn y recortey cooidjagh 'sy seyrlan.

lessons.title: Yn daunseyr ballay
lessons.summary: Fourteen-year-old Emmeline Dacre dances ballet in Douglas with her teacher Sabine Moreau, though ballet is not fashionable among her school friends; she is a good jumper and loves turning on one foot, and she practises kicking her leg high; before the show her foot hurts and her toes are bruised, and Sabine tells her that health comes first and she must rest for a week; on the night her white costume, stiff with starch and closed with small fasteners at the back, is ready, her foot is better and she dances well.
lessons.text:
Ta Emmeline Dacre kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash, as t'ee daunsey ballay. Dagh Jesarn, t'ee goll gys scoill ballay ayns Doolish. She Sabine Moreau yn ynseyder eck.

Cha nel ballay fassanagh mastey ny caarjyn eck 'sy scoill. Ta ny caarjyn eck cloie bluckan-coshey, ny t'ad eaishtagh rish kiaull fassanagh. Agh cha nel Emmeline laccal ve fassanagh. S'mie lhee ballay.

Ta Emmeline ny lheimmeyder mie. T'ee jannoo lheimyn ard, as t'ee çheet sheese dy aashagh. “T'ou ny lheimmeyder share 'sy scoill,” ta Sabine gra.

S'mie lhee çhyndaays neesht. T'ee shassoo er un chass, as t'ee çhyndaa, çhyndaa, çhyndaa. Ta Sabine gra dy vel yn çhyndaays eck aalin. Ta Emmeline jannoo brebbal neesht: t'ee brebbal lesh e cass, ard 'syn aer, as eisht t'ee brebbal lesh y chass elley.

Shiaghtin roish y chloie vooar, va guinn ayns cass Emmeline. Ren ee jeeaghyn er e cass. Va mairyn e coshey broojit as gorrym. “Ta'n chass aym broojit,” dooyrt ee rish Sabine. “As ta guinn trome ayn.”

Ren Sabine jeeaghyn er y chass. “Eaisht rish shoh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n follanid ayd ny smoo scanshoil na ballay. Follanid hoshiaght, eisht daunsey. Cha jean oo daunsey rish shiaghtin.”

Va Emmeline trimshagh, agh ren ee myr dooyrt Sabine. Hug ee ushtey feayr er e cass dagh laa.

Er y laa roish y chloie, hie Emmeline gys y scoill dy jeeaghyn er yn eaddagh eck. Va'n eaddagh bane, as va stark ayn. Va'n stark cur er dy hassoo magh mygeayrt ee. Va dooneyderyn beggey er y cooyl echey. Ren Sabine ny dooneyderyn y ghooney.

“Cha nel eh aashagh dy ve ayns yn eaddagh shoh,” dooyrt Emmeline. “Ta'n stark cur er ve creoi.”

“Ta,” dooyrt Sabine. “Agh t'eh aalin.”

Er oie y chloie, cha row guinn ayns cass Emmeline. Cha row mairyn e coshey broojit ny smoo. Ren ee lheimyn ard, as çhyndaa, as brebbal. Va'n çhyndaays eck aalin. Ren yn ynseyder eck gearey.

Feyshtyn:
Vel ballay fassanagh mastey caarjyn Emmeline?
Cha nel. Cha nel ballay fassanagh mastey ny caarjyn eck.
Quoi ta gra dy vel Emmeline ny lheimmeyder mie?
Ta Sabine Moreau, yn ynseyder eck, gra shen.
Kys va mairyn e coshey?
Va mairyn e coshey broojit as gorrym, as va guinn ayns e cass.
Cre dooyrt Sabine mychione follanid?
Dooyrt ee dy vel y follanid ny smoo scanshoil na ballay.
Cre va er y cooyl jeh'n eaddagh?
Va dooneyderyn beggey er y cooyl echey.

lessons.title: Rein ny h-Oie
lessons.summary: Marigold Stannard takes her ten-year-old son Aldous to see Mozart's opera with the magic flute at the Gaiety Theatre in Douglas; the stage is dark, a big monster like a snake chases the young prince Tamino, and Aldous is a little afraid; the Queen of the Night sings very high; the story is full of supernatural things; Sarastro's temple has lanterns and heavenly music, like paradise; Tamino must keep silence and show obedience in his tests; in the end the dark goes and the light comes, and Aldous wants to come back.
lessons.text:
Va Marigold Stannard as e vac Aldous ayns y thie-cloie mooar ayns Doolish. Ta Aldous jeih bleeaney d'eash. Va kiaulldramey Mozart ayn: skeeal mychione feddan obbee.

Haink tostid er y thie-cloie. Va'n ardan keeir. Eisht haink y kiaull. Ren dooinney aeg roie er yn ardan. She prinse va ayn, as Tamino yn ennym echey. Va beisht vooar roie ny yei. Va'n veisht gollrish aarnieu, as va ny sooillyn eck jiarg.

Va aggle beggan er Aldous. “Vel y veisht shen feer?” dooyrt eh.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt e voir. “She skeeal neuheiltagh t'ayn. Ta ymmodee reddyn neuheiltagh ayn: feddan obbee, ushagyn loayrtagh, as rein.”

Lurg tammylt, va'n ardan keeir reesht, as haink yn rein. She Rein ny h-Oie v'ayn. Va eaddagh doo urree, as va rollageyn er yn eaddagh. Ren y rein goaill arrane. Va'n coraa eck feer ard, ny syrjey na coraa erbee ta Aldous er chlashtyn. Va inneen ec Rein ny h-Oie, Pamina, as dooyrt y rein rish Tamino dy gheddyn ee.

'Sy nah ayrn, va çhiamble Sarastro er yn ardan. Va londeyryn soilshagh ayns y çhiamble, as va soilshey çheet ass ny londeyryn. Ren ny arraneyderyn goaill arrane flaunyssagh. Va'n kiaull flaunyssagh as meein.

“Ta shoh myr pargys,” dooyrt Marigold. “Ta'n çhiamble myr pargys, lane soilshey as kiaull flaunyssagh.”

Eisht va teishtyn ec Tamino. Va'n chied teisht tostid: cha by chair da loayrt fockle. Haink Pamina, as loayr ee rish, agh cha dooyrt eh veg. Va tostid echey. Va Pamina trimshagh.

Va biallys ayns ny teishtyn neesht. Ren Tamino ooilley myr dooyrt Sarastro rish. “Ta biallys scanshoil 'sy skeeal shoh,” dooyrt Marigold. “Ta biallys as tostid cur niart da Tamino.”

Ec y jerrey, cha row yn ardan keeir ny smoo. Hie Rein ny h-Oie ersooyl, as haink y soilshey. Va'n skeeal neuheiltagh harrish. Va Tamino as Pamina ayns pargys dy chiaull.

Va tostid ayns y thie-cloie son tammylt beg. Eisht ren y sleih ooilley bwoalley nyn laueyn.

“Vel shin çheet reesht?” dooyrt Aldous. “Ta mee laccal fakin y veisht reesht!”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n kiaulldramey va ayns y thie-cloie?
Va kiaulldramey Mozart ayn, skeeal mychione feddan obbee.
Kys va'n veisht jeeaghyn?
Va'n veisht gollrish aarnieu, as va ny sooillyn eck jiarg.
Cre'n eaddagh va er Rein ny h-Oie?
Va eaddagh doo urree, lesh rollageyn er.
Cre va ayns y çhiamble?
Va londeyryn soilshagh ayns y çhiamble.
Cre va'n chied teisht ec Tamino?
Va'n chied teisht tostid: cha by chair da loayrt fockle.

lessons.title: Arrane y çhennid
lessons.summary: At a folk festival in Peel the singer Cyprian Yelland explains an old ballad before he sings it: a foreign baron laid siege to the castle of a duchess for six months; disease came into the castle; then a woman came to the gateway and said she was a witch with a plant against the disease, but it was a fraud: she was the baron's soldier in a witch's clothes and wanted to steal the duchess's gold and open the gateway; the duchess saw the deceit, kept the gateway shut, and the baron went home; Cyprian sings, and the people sing with him at the end.
lessons.text:
Va feaill kiaull ayns Purt ny h-Inshey. Va ymmodee sleih ayns y thie mooar faggys da'n traie. Haink Cyprian Yelland er yn ardan lesh gitar. She arraneyder eh, as t'eh goaill shenn arraneyn.

“Ta'n arrane shoh feer shenn,” dooyrt eh. “She arrane mychione çhennid t'ayn. Lhig dou yn skeeal y insh diu hoshiaght.”

Va'n sleih eaishtagh.

“Keayrt dy row, va bendiuic cummal ayns cashtal faggys da'n aarkey. Va'n vendiuic aeg as lajer. Haink barran joaree lesh sidooryn veih'n çheer elley. Va'n barran joaree laccal y cashtal, son va airh ec y vendiuic.

“Ren y barran çhennid er y chashtal. Va'n çhennid liauyr: rish shey meeaghyn, cha dod peiagh erbee goll stiagh ny çheet magh. Ec y jerrey, haink aacheoid 'sy chashtal. Va ymmodee sleih ching, as hooar paart jeu baase jeh'n aacheoid.

“Un oie, haink ben gys doarlish y chashtal. ‘She buitçh mish,’ dooyrt ee. ‘Ta lus aym noi'n aacheoid. Foshil y doarlish, as ver-ym yn lus diu.’

“Agh she molteyrys v'ayn. Cha nee buitçh v'ayn. She fer jeh sidooryn y barran joaree v'ayn, ayns eaddagh buitçh. V'eh laccal yn airh y gheid, as v'eh laccal y doarlish y osley da ny sidooryn elley.

“Ren y vendiuic jeeaghyn er eddin y ven, as honnick ee y molteyrys. ‘Cha nee buitçh oo,’ dooyrt ee. ‘She joaree oo, as t'ou laccal my airh y gheid.’ Cha ren ee y doarlish y osley.

“Lurg shen, hie y barran thie. Cha row eh kionyssagh er y chashtal. Va'n vendiuic kionyssagh ayns e cashtal hene. Hie yn aacheoid ersooyl 'sy tourey, as va'n sleih slane reesht.”

Eisht ren Cyprian yn arrane y ghoaill. Va'n arrane liauyr, lesh ymmodee raaghyn. Ec y jerrey, ren ny sleih goaill y raa jerrinagh marish: “Cha jean y joaree yn airh y gheid, as cha bee eh kionyssagh 'sy chashtal.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va cummal 'sy chashtal?
Va bendiuic cummal 'sy chashtal faggys da'n aarkey.
Cre ren y barran joaree?
Ren eh çhennid er y chashtal rish shey meeaghyn.
Cre haink 'sy chashtal ec y jerrey?
Haink aacheoid 'sy chashtal, as va ymmodee sleih ching.
Quoi haink gys y doarlish?
Haink ben gys y doarlish, as dooyrt ee dy row ee ny buitçh.
Cre'n molteyrys v'ayn?
She fer jeh sidooryn y barran v'ayn, ayns eaddagh buitçh. V'eh laccal yn airh y gheid.

lessons.title: Kiaull ayns y thie oast
lessons.summary: Jemima Varley keeps an inn by the fishing harbour in Port Erin and brews her own beer from barley and a herb that also works as a preservative; every Thursday people from the neighbourhood come to play music; one Thursday Fiachra Mulholland, a whistle player from the east coast of Ireland who works in the fish trade between Ireland and the island, joins them; the new beer is ready, the waste barley goes to a farmer's pigs, a dog chews a bone under the table, and Fiachra promises to come back.
lessons.text:
Ta thie oast ec Jemima Varley ayns Purt Çhiarn, faggys da'n phurt eeastee. Ta baatyn eeastee 'sy phurt, as ta ny eeasteyryn çheet gys y thie oast 'syn astyr.

Ta Jemima imbyl y lhune eck hene. T'ee jannoo y lhune ass oarn. Ta'n oarn çheet veih thie-ollee faggys da'n valley. T'ee cur luss stiagh 'sy lhune neesht, son blass. Ta'n luss gaase ayns y gharey eck. “Ta'n luss shoh cur blass millish da'n lhune,” t'ee gra. “As she freaylleyder t'ayn neesht. Ta'n freaylleyder freayll y lhune mie son tammylt liauyr.”

Dagh Jerdein, ta kiaull ayns y thie oast. Ta sleih veih'n naboonys çheet lesh nyn gitaryn as nyn feddanyn. Ta ny sleih ooilley 'sy naboonys enney er y cheilley.

Un Jerdein, haink dooinney noa stiagh. Va feddan ayns e laue. “Fiachra Mulholland ta mee,” dooyrt eh. “Ta mee veih Nerin.”

“C'raad ayns Nerin?” dooyrt Jemima.

“Ta mee cummal ayns balley beg er yn oirr shiar,” dooyrt Fiachra. “Ta mee gobbraghey ayns cochionneeaght eeast. Ta mee kionnaghey eeast 'sy phurt eeastee shoh, as ta mee creck eh ayns Nerin. Ta'n chochionneeaght shoh mie dou.”

Ren Fiachra soie marish ny kiaulleyderyn, as ren eh cloie. Va'n kiaull echey tappee as aalin. Ren ny sleih ooilley eaishtagh.

Va moddey beg fo'n voayrd, as v'eh caigney craue. Va'n moddey caigney as caigney, as cha ren eh eaishtagh rish y kiaull.

Lurg tammylt, dooyrt Jemima: “Ta'n lhune noa aarloo! Ren mee imbyl eh rish three shiaghtinyn, as t'eh aarloo nish.” Hug ee lhune da dagh peiagh.

“Cre ta oo jannoo lesh yn oarn lurg yn imbyl?” dooyrt Fiachra.

“Cha nel jeeyll ayn,” dooyrt Jemima. “Ta'n oarn goll gys eirinagh 'sy naboonys, son ny muckyn echey. Ta ny muckyn gee eh ooilley, as cha nel jeeyll erbee ayn.”

Ren Fiachra gearey. “Ta'n lhune shoh ny share na lhune erbee ayns Nerin,” dooyrt eh.

Ec y jerrey, ghow Fiachra baatey erash gys Nerin. “Bee mee aarloo dy heet reesht,” dooyrt eh, “tra ta'n chochionneeaght gymmyrkey mee gys y phurt shoh.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ass ta Jemima jannoo yn lhune?
T'ee jannoo yn lhune ass oarn, as t'ee cur luss stiagh ayn son blass, as myr freaylleyder.
C'raad ta Fiachra cummal?
T'eh cummal ayns balley beg er oirr shiar Nerin.
Cre'n obbyr ta ec Fiachra?
T'eh gobbraghey ayns cochionneeaght eeast.
Cre va'n moddey jannoo fo'n voayrd?
V'eh caigney craue.
Cre ta Jemima jannoo lesh yn oarn lurg yn imbyl?
T'ee cur yn oarn da eirinagh 'sy naboonys, son ny muckyn echey. Cha nel jeeyll erbee ayn.

lessons.title: Kiaull y vagher
lessons.summary: The composer Gwendolen Ormerod is writing a piece of music about a summer meadow, and she takes her nine-year-old daughter Ellery to listen by an old hedge near Sulby; they sit on the turf and hear swifts screaming in the sky, lambs in the next field and a fly near Ellery's ear; Ellery watches butterflies and a hairy bee, and finds a white flower in an umbel with yellow anthers and a downy leaf; at home Gwendolen writes a part for each sound, and calls the piece after the hedge.
lessons.text:
Ta Gwendolen Ormerod ny cummeyder kiaull. T'ee screeu peesh kiaull noa mychione magher 'sy tourey. Er laa çheh, ghow ee e inneen Ellery lhee gys magher faggys da Sulby. Ta Ellery nuy bleeaney d'eash.

Va cleiy shenn er oirr y vagher, lesh blaaghyn ayn. Ren Gwendolen as Ellery soie er y foaid faggys da cleiy y vagher. Va'n foaid bog as glass.

“Ny loayr,” dooyrt Gwendolen. “Eaisht.”

Ren Ellery eaishtagh. Hoshiaght, ren ee clashtyn ushagyn 'syn aer. Va gollanyn etlagh harrish y vagher, ard as tappee. “Ta ny gollanyn eam!” dooyrt Ellery. “She gollanyn t'ayn,” dooyrt e moir. “T'ad çheet veih'n Affrick dagh blein.”

Eisht ren ad clashtyn eayin 'sy nah vagher. Va eayn beg eam son e voir. Va ny eayin roie mygeayrt.

Haink quaillag faggys da cleaysh Ellery. Va'n quaillag cur magh sheean. Hug Ellery y quaillag ersooyl lesh e laue.

Va follicanyn er ny blaaghyn er y cleiy. Va follican bane as follican buigh ayn. Ren Ellery jeeaghyn er ny follicanyn son tammylt liauyr. Haink shellan neesht. Va'n shellan foltagh as doo as buigh. “Ta'n shellan foltagh!” dooyrt Ellery. “T'ee myr kayt beg.”

Hooar Ellery blaa bane er y cleiy. Va ny blaaghyn beggey cooidjagh ayns umbyl, myr scaa-fliaghee. “She umbyl t'ayn,” dooyrt Gwendolen. “Ta ymmodee blaaghyn beggey ayns un umbyl.”

Ren Ellery jeeaghyn er y blaa dy faggys. Va red buigh ayns mean y vlaa. “Cre shoh?” dooyrt ee. “She anthyryn t'ayn,” dooyrt e moir. “Ta ny anthyryn lane dy yoan buigh.” Va duillag y vlaa fynnagh neesht. Ren Ellery y duillag fynnagh y ghoaill ayns e laue. Va'n duillag fynnagh bog, myr crackan eayn.

Tra hie ad thie, ren Gwendolen soie ec y phianney. Ren ee ayrn y screeu son dagh sheean: ayrn son ny gollanyn, ayrn son ny eayin, as ayrn beg son y quaillag. Ren ee ayrn aalin son ny follicanyn neesht.

“Cre'n ennym t'ec y kiaull?” dooyrt Ellery.

“Kiaull y Cleiy,” dooyrt Gwendolen. “Ta bea ayns y cleiy shenn, as ta kiaull ayn.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ren Gwendolen as Ellery soie?
Ren ad soie er y foaid faggys da cleiy y vagher.
Cre va eam harrish y vagher?
Va gollanyn eam harrish y vagher.
Cre va 'sy nah vagher?
Va eayin 'sy nah vagher.
Kys va'n shellan?
Va'n shellan foltagh as doo as buigh.
Cre va ayns mean y vlaa?
Va anthyryn buigh ayns mean y vlaa.

lessons.title: Y greie kiaull gyn bentyn
lessons.summary: Sixteen-year-old Anatole Bellingham builds a theremin for a school science project with his physics teacher Nathaniel Oakes, who tells him about its Russian inventor; the machine has two metal rods, a light magnesium box and a lithium battery; the rods radiate a field, and the player changes the sound by moving his hands near them without touching; when Anatole's two hands are too near, the sounds collide and the sound is sharp; on the computer they make an analysis of the sound waves, and Anatole plays a slow song for the class.
lessons.text:
Ta Anatole Bellingham shey bleeaney jeig d'eash. T'eh gobbraghey er obbyr-scoill çhaghnoaylleeagh. T'eh laccal greie kiaull y yannoo: theremin. Ta Nathaniel Oakes, yn ynseyder fishig echey, gobbraghey marish.

“Quoi va'n feddynagh?” dooyrt Anatole.

“Va'n feddynagh veih'n Roosh,” dooyrt Nathaniel. “Theremin va'n ennym echey. She feddynagh mie v'ayn. Ren eh y greie shoh 'sy vlein 1920. Va'n theremin yn chied greie kiaull çhaghnoaylleeagh as lectragh.”

Ta daa slat yiarn er y theremin. Ta'n kishtey jeant jeh magnaishum. Ta magnaishum eddrym, as myr shen, cha nel y kishtey trome. Ta bree çheet veih litçhey. “Ta litçhey 'sy chishtey,” dooyrt Nathaniel. “Ta'n litçhey cur bree da'n theremin.”

“Kys ta mee cloie er?” dooyrt Anatole.

“Cha nel oo bentyn rish,” dooyrt Nathaniel. “Ta ny slattyn goulraghey. Ta'n goulraghey jannoo ynnyd lectragh mygeayrt y slat. Tra ta dty laue çheet faggys da'n slat, ta'n sheean caghlaa.”

Ren Anatole e laue y chur faggys da'n slat. Haink sheean ard. Ren eh e laue y ghoaill ersooyl, as va'n sheean ny s'inshley. Va'n sheean quaagh, myr coraa ben ayns kiaulldramey.

Eisht ren eh e laueyn ooilley y chur faggys da ny slattyn. Va ny laueyn echey ro faggys. Ren ny sheeanyn covuilley. Va'n sheean foyragh as garroo. “Ta ny sheeanyn covuilley!” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n sheean foyragh.”

“Ta,” dooyrt Nathaniel, gearey. “Cha nel sheean foyragh mie son arrane.”

Ren ad mynscrutaghey er y sheean er y co-earrooder. Ren y co-earrooder jalloo jeh ny tonnyn. “Shoh mynscrutaghey jeh'n sheean,” dooyrt Nathaniel. “Jeeagh: tra ta'n sheean foyragh, ta ny tonnyn beg as tappee.”

Er y Jeheiney, ren Anatole y theremin y ghoaill gys y scoill. Ren eh cloie arrane moal da'n rang. Cha ren eh bentyn rish y greie un cheayrt. Ren y rang ooilley eaishtagh, as cha dooyrt peiagh erbee fockle.

“Ta'n theremin çhaghnoaylleeagh,” dooyrt Anatole ec y jerrey, “agh ta'n kiaull çheet ass ny laueyn.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va feddynagh y theremin?
Va'n feddynagh veih'n Roosh, as Theremin yn ennym echey.
Cre jeh ta'n kishtey jeant?
Ta'n kishtey jeant jeh magnaishum.
Cre ta cur bree da'n theremin?
Ta litçhey cur bree da'n theremin.
Cre ta ny slattyn jannoo?
Ta ny slattyn goulraghey.
Kys va'n sheean tra ren ny sheeanyn covuilley?
Va'n sheean foyragh as garroo.
Cre ren ad er y co-earrooder?
Ren ad mynscrutaghey er y sheean.

lessons.title: Lettyr veih'n ghrianchryss
lessons.summary: In a letter to her brother Ingram in Ramsey, the anthropologist Felicity Hesketh writes from a village by a lagoon in the tropics, where she records the songs of the fishermen's families; last year she recorded songs on the cold tundra in the far north, where few places are habitable; here locusts came and ate the fields, and there is a song against them; the dry sand sucks up the rain; the lagoon is only two metres deep, and pollution from a new factory is harming the fish, so the people sing about clean water.
lessons.text:
Ingram veen,

Ta mee screeu hood veih'n ghrianchryss. Ta mee ayns balley beg er oirr mooirlagh mooar. Ta'n emshir feer çheh. Ta fys ayd dy vel mee gobbraghey ayns antrapoaylleeaght: ta mee studeyrys sleih as nyn mea. Ayns y vlein shoh, ta mee recortey arraneyn sleih y valley. She antrapoaylleeaght kiaull t'ayn.

Blein er dy henney, va mee er y tundrey 'sy twoaie. V'eh feer feayr er y tundrey. Cha nel ymmodee buill baghagh ayn: ta rio er y thalloo son y chooid smoo jeh'n vlein. Ta'n sleih ta cummal er y tundrey goaill arraneyn moal as liauyr. Ta'n ghrianchryss feer anchasley: ta'n aer çheh as fliugh, as ta'n balley shoh feer vaghagh, lesh bee as ushtey dy liooar.

Ta'n sleih ayns y balley shoh nyn eeasteyryn. T'ad goll magh er y mooirlagh ayns baatyn beggey. Cha nel y mooirlagh dowin: cha nel eh agh daa veedyr, as ayns ynnydyn, cha nel eh agh un veedyr. Tra t'ad tayrn y lieen, t'ad goaill arrane cooidjagh.

Mee er dy henney, haink locust gys y balley. Va'n locust 'syn aer myr bodjal doo, as ren eh ny magheryn y ee. Ren y locust dagh duillag glass y ee. Ta arrane ec y sleih noi'n locust. Ren mee yn arrane shen y recortey neesht.

Ta'n thalloo çhirrym ayns shoh. Tra ta'n fliaghey çheet, ta'n geinnagh jiole yn ushtey. Ta'n geinnagh jiole yn fliaghey ooilley ayns minnid. Cha nel ushtey er y thalloo lurg oor.

Agh ta boirey ayn. Ta thie-jeant noa faggys da'n mooirlagh. Ta sollaghey çheet veih'n thie-jeant stiagh 'sy mooirlagh. Ta'n sollaghey jannoo assee da ny eeastyn. Ta ny eeasteyryn trimshagh. T'ad er screeu arrane noa mychione y sollaghey, as mychione ushtey glen. Shen yn arrane share t'ayn, er my hon's.

Hig mee thie 'sy nah vee. Ver-ym lhiam ny arraneyn ooilley.

Lesh graih,
Felicity

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta Felicity cummal nish?
T'ee cummal ayns balley beg er oirr mooirlagh ayns y ghrianchryss.
Cre'n obbyr t'ec Felicity?
T'ee gobbraghey ayns antrapoaylleeaght, as t'ee recortey arraneyn.
Vel ymmodee buill baghagh er y tundrey?
Cha nel. Ta rio er y thalloo son y chooid smoo jeh'n vlein.
Vel y mooirlagh dowin?
Cha nel. Cha nel eh agh daa veedyr, as ayns ynnydyn un veedyr.
Cre ren y locust?
Ren y locust ny magheryn y ee.
Cre ta'n sollaghey jannoo?
Ta'n sollaghey jannoo assee da ny eeastyn 'sy mooirlagh.

lessons.title: Y fockleyreyder as y rabbi
lessons.summary: The lexicographer Abel Danby is writing a Manx dictionary of music words in the library in Douglas, which was rebuilt after a fire; he has made a survey of musicians on the island to learn which words they use; he is allergic to dust, so old books make his eyes red; one day Rabbi Joachim Mendel comes to the library looking for an old book of songs that a Jewish family left there long ago; they find it on a dusty shelf, the rabbi sings a song from it, and Abel asks him about the words for his dictionary.
lessons.text:
Ta Abel Danby ny fockleyreyder. T'eh screeu fockleyr: fockleyr dy ockleyn kiaull ayns Gaelg. T'eh gobbraghey 'sy lioarlan ayns Doolish dagh laa.

Ta'n lioarlan shenn, agh ta'n thie noa. Va aile 'sy lioarlan jeih bleeaney er dy henney, as va'n thie aahroggit lurg yn aile. Ren y sleih y lioarlan y aahrog lesh claghyn y shenn thie. Ta'n lioarlan aahroggit soilshagh as mooar.

Ren Abel creear er kiaulleyderyn ayns Ellan Vannin. Hug eh feyshtyn da keead kiaulleyder: “Cre ny focklyn ayns Gaelg t'ou jannoo ymmyd jeu son kiaull?” Ec y jerrey, va keead freggyrt echey. Ta'n creear scanshoil son y fockleyr. Ta ymmodee focklyn noa ayns y creear.

Agh ta boirey ec Abel. T'eh allerjagh noi joan. Ta joan dy liooar er ny shenn lioaryn 'sy lioarlan. Tra t'eh fosley shenn lioar, ta ny sooillyn echey jiarg. “Ta mee allerjagh,” t'eh gra, “as ta mee gobbraghey ayns lioarlan! T'eh myr eeasteyr nagh vel laccal ushtey.”

Un laa, haink dooinney stiagh 'sy lioarlan. Va eaddagh doo er, as va lioar ayns e laue. “Joachim Mendel ta mee,” dooyrt eh. “She rabbi mish, veih Manchester. Ta shenn lioar arraneyn ayns y lioarlan shoh, ta mee credjal. Daag lught-thie ennagh y lioar ayns shoh keead bleeaney er dy henney.”

Ren y fockleyreyder as y rabbi ronsaghey cooidjagh. Ec y jerrey, hooar ad y lioar er shelloo ard. Va joan trome urree. Va sooillyn Abel jiarg reesht.

Ren y rabbi y lioar y osley. Va'n screeu ayns çhengey shenn. Ren y rabbi gearey. “She shoh ee!” dooyrt eh. Eisht ren y rabbi arrane y ghoaill veih'n lioar. Va'n coraa echey dowin as aalin. Va tostid 'sy lioarlan, as ren ooilley ny lhaihderyn eaishtagh.

“Cre ta'n arrane gra?” dooyrt Abel.

“T'eh gra dy vel kiaull myr soilshey 'sy dorraghey,” dooyrt y rabbi.

Ren y fockleyreyder screeu ny focklyn shen 'sy lioar echey. “Ta fockle noa aym son y fockleyr,” dooyrt eh.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Abel Danby jannoo?
She fockleyreyder eh. T'eh screeu fockleyr dy ockleyn kiaull.
Cre'n fa ta'n lioarlan noa?
Va aile ayn, as va'n thie aahroggit lurg yn aile.
Cre'n creear ren Abel?
Hug eh feyshtyn da keead kiaulleyder ayns Ellan Vannin.
Cre'n fa ta sooillyn Abel jiarg?
T'eh allerjagh noi joan.
Quoi haink stiagh 'sy lioarlan?
Haink Joachim Mendel, rabbi veih Manchester.
